label: clean
conclusion: A misplaced decimal point made spinach famous as an iron-rich food.
premises: Published analyses of spinach's iron content from the early twentieth century reported a value approximately ten times higher than the amount measured by later analyses.

The tenfold overstatement of spinach's iron content in the nutrition literature originated from a decimal point placed one position too far to the right when the original measurement was recorded or transcribed.
Raw spinach contains roughly 2.7 mg of iron per 100 g, a level comparable to other common leafy green vegetables rather than exceptional among foods.
The overstated iron figure for spinach was reproduced in food composition tables, textbooks, and popular media for decades before being corrected.

Popular belief that spinach is an exceptionally iron-rich food emerged after the erroneous figure entered circulation and was not supported by any independent measurement showing unusually high iron in spinach.
A food is famous as iron-rich when the public widely believes it to contain unusually high amounts of iron relative to other foods.
note: passed the eyeball review; see review_flags for what it passed with

label: clean
conclusion: Goldfish have a memory span of three seconds.
premises: Memory span is defined as the maximum time interval over which an animal can retain learned information such that it still influences the animal's behavior.
In conditioning experiments, goldfish demonstrate retention of a learned association when the retention interval is three seconds or shorter.

The three-second retention limit measured in laboratory goldfish is characteristic of the species as a whole rather than of particular individuals or testing conditions.

label: blind-spot
conclusion: Humans use only ten percent of their brains.
premises: Approximately ten percent of the neurons in a human brain are engaged in functional activity, and the remaining ninety percent are never engaged.

Functional neuroimaging of humans performing cognitive, sensory, and motor tasks reveals measurable activation confined to roughly one tenth of total brain volume, with the rest showing no task-related activity.
Damage to or surgical removal of the brain regions that are not functionally engaged produces no detectable deficit in perception, movement, cognition, or behavior.
For an organ, to 'use' a portion of it means that portion is engaged in performing some function.
The metabolic energy consumed by the human brain corresponds to the activity of about one tenth of its tissue rather than the whole organ.
The proportion of the brain that is functionally engaged is essentially the same across healthy adult humans, so a single figure characterizes the species.
